sections.h2: What should a Princeton seller know about how Caldwell County taxes a house?
sections.html:
The local Property Valuation Administrator values the house, the Caldwell County Sheriff collects the money, and anything unpaid after April 15 goes to the clerk. Values are fixed as of January 1, and the Department of Revenue says the PVA must walk every parcel at least once in four years, as described on its real property assessment page.

Princeton anchors a county of roughly 345 square miles of land. A Caldwell bill adds together several taxing districts, among them the state, the county and the schools, and each of those bodies picks its own rate. The assessor has no say over rates.

The county has long been farm country. Farmland is taxed on what it can produce rather than on market price. The sheriff's site says a parcel of ten or more acres used for livestock or crops, timber included, can qualify, so an owner with acreage should ask the PVA how the land is carried before listing.

sections.h2: Which dates and penalties apply to a Caldwell County tax bill?
sections.html:
The payment year runs on a fixed monthly ladder that starts on November 1 and ends on April 15. The sheriff's tax page lays out the steps, and the statewide framework behind them is KRS 134.015.

Collection for 2026 opened November 2, 2026, after bills were mailed October 30, and the sheriff replaced postcards with letter-style bills. Whatever the phase, a payment is credited if it is postmarked, handed over or dropped in the box before the next phase begins. The ladder looks like this:

  • All of November: the bill less 2%.
  • All of December: the bare face amount.
  • All of January: 5% extra.
  • February 1 through April 15: 21% extra.

The office is the first door to the right off Main Street inside the Princeton courthouse. It takes checks, money orders, cashier's checks, cash and, at the counter, cards with a processing surcharge. A drop box by the east courthouse door handles after-hours payments, with no cash allowed. Hours run 8 am to 4 pm on weekdays, and the sheriff posts a holiday closing list each season.

sections.h2: Which Caldwell County office answers which tax question?
sections.html:
Three numbers cover almost every question: 270-365-2088 for the sheriff, 270-365-7227 for the PVA and 270-365-6754 for the clerk. The PVA is on the courthouse's second floor at 100 East Market Street, and the sheriff takes mail at Room 25 of the same building.

  • Sheriff: mails bills, accepts payment until April 15, and runs a view-only bill search online.
  • PVA: sets values, takes homestead and disability forms, and holds the conference that must come before an appeal.
  • County clerk: takes over delinquent bills and records deeds.

The bill is addressed to whoever owned the parcel on January 1. A buyer whose bill went to the previous owner can print it from the sheriff's site, and the sheriff, who does not receive deed transfers, lists the new name in care-of form the first year.

sections.h2: How can a Princeton owner dispute a Caldwell County value?
sections.html:
Book a conference with the PVA first, then file at the clerk's office no later than the workday after public inspection ends. Inspection lasts 13 days from the first Monday in May, and the local appeals board sits up to five days beginning 25 to 35 days later, as the state property tax calendar explains.

Bring facts, not opinions. Useful evidence includes lot and building descriptions, insurance papers, what the house cost to build and listings of comparable sales. An appeal without that paper is denied. Skipping the local board also closes the door to later review. Because bills can print before a case ends, the value you claim is billed in the meantime, and a supplemental bill arrives if the board lands higher.

Whatever number survives is what a buyer's lender and title company will see. A Princeton owner whose house has gained a new roof or an addition should check that the PVA's record describes the house as it stands.

sections.h2: Which relief programs lower a Caldwell County bill?
sections.html:
Owner-occupants who are 65 or older, or totally disabled, can have part of the assessed value removed. The sheriff's page puts the maximum at $46,350 for 2024 and 2025, and KRS 132.810 resets it every two years, so the PVA can quote today's figure.

Applicants must live in the house they own, prove their age and claim no exemption elsewhere. The form is completed at the PVA office, which the sheriff says takes under five minutes. The benefit stays with the owner, so whoever buys from you files separately.

An older seller should confirm the exemption shows on the bill before closing. The sheriff asks owners to sort out a missing exemption with the PVA before paying.

sections.h2: What happens to the Caldwell County bill at closing?
sections.html:
The lien stays with the parcel while the closing agent splits the year between the two sides. According to the sheriff's FAQ, your agent or lender explains the split, since the sheriff is never told how a sale handled it.

Unpaid bills stay alive after a sale. Delinquent bills move to the clerk with penalties and 1% monthly interest, as the Department of Revenue's collection process page shows. A Princeton owner with back taxes should get the clerk's payoff figure before picking a closing date.

Where a lender escrows taxes, the bill still goes to the owner, and the sheriff says forwarding it is the owner's job. Checking in with the servicer now and then keeps a missed forward from becoming a penalty.

sections.h2: Who is buying and selling homes in Caldwell County?
sections.html:
Caldwell County has about 12,600 residents, and its typical owner-occupied home is valued at $118,500 for 2020 to 2024, far under Campbell County in northern Kentucky. Princeton, with 6,270 people in 2020, grew up around railroad junctions. It hosts a University of Kentucky research campus, factories such as Bremner provide jobs, and a December 2021 tornado hit the south side of town.

Roughly 30 percent of occupied homes here are rentals, and 93.4 percent of residents had not moved in the past year, so few houses change hands. Those that do often belong to estates, older owners or farm families, and an owner facing repairs or a tenant may prefer a direct cash sale to skip showings.

faqs.q: What dates matter for Caldwell County tax bills?
faqs.a: The bill opens for payment on November 1, and the 2% discount lasts through November 30. December is face value, January adds 5% and February 1 to April 15 adds 21%. Anything still open on April 15 goes to the county clerk.

faqs.q: Where can I pay a tax bill in Princeton?
faqs.a: Go to the sheriff's office in the courthouse, mail to 100 E. Market St., Room 25, or use the drop box at the east door. The website search only displays bills, and phone payments are not taken.

faqs.q: Is there a tax break for homeowners over 65 in Caldwell County?
faqs.a: Yes, the homestead exemption covers owners who live in the home and turn 65 during the year. Apply at the PVA office with proof of age. It trims the assessed value, and a new owner must apply again.

faqs.q: What if my Princeton house sells before the bill comes?
faqs.a: The bill is issued to the January 1 owner, so you may still get it. The closing agent prorates, and a buyer who never receives it can print a copy from the sheriff's site.

faqs.q: Do I need repairs before a cash sale in Caldwell County?
faqs.a: No. A cash buyer can take the house as-is. Back taxes and liens come out of your proceeds, so ask the sheriff and clerk for amounts early.
